q: How does a garment factory in Sri Lanka's Katunayake zone work out Scope 2?
title: Katunayake garment factory: Scope 2
short: kWh from monthly electricity bills times Sri Lanka's grid factor for the year, which moves with how much hydro ran versus coal and oil. Rooftop solar used on site cuts the kWh bought. Report location based Scope 2, and market based too if you buy renewable certificates.
audience: Apparel factories in Katunayake, Biyagama and other Sri Lankan export zones

ol: Multiply by the grid factor for the year, with its source.
Report solar generated and used separately.

p: A wet year with more hydro lowers the factor; a dry year leans on the coal plant and oil. Do not reuse an old figure.
Most large brands ask for monthly energy and renewable share, often through their own platform.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity, fuel and boiler invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per factory, so the figures a brand asks for can be traced back to the bills.

sources.label: International Energy Agency, country energy data (iea.org)
